meta.title: Source Library
meta.description: The evidentiary base of the record: courts, UN bodies, human rights organisations, peer-reviewed research, open datasets, declassified archives and the Israeli press. Sources are grouped by the weight they carry, not by convenience. Every claim in the report is anchored to a source of one of these classes.
meta.note: Where a link is given it points to the authoritative publisher, not to an aggregator. Where no link is given the source is a print or archival record cited in the report's bibliography.

groups.label: Courts and tribunals
groups.blurb: Judgments, orders and advisory opinions. The highest evidentiary class in this record: findings of fact and law by the bodies competent to make them. Domestic judgments are listed here only where a question raised in this record has actually been litigated to judgment in a national court.

items.title: Legal Consequences of the Construction of a Wall in the Occupied Palestinian Territory
items.note: Advisory Opinion. Held the wall and the settlement enterprise contrary to international law and affirmed the applicability of the Fourth Geneva Convention to the occupied territory.

items.title: Application of the Genocide Convention (South Africa v. Israel) — Order on Provisional Measures
items.note: Found it plausible that the acts complained of fall within the Genocide Convention; ordered Israel to prevent and punish direct and public incitement to genocide. Measures strengthened 28 March and 24 May 2024.

items.title: Legal Consequences arising from the Policies and Practices of Israel in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem
items.note: Advisory Opinion. The occupation is unlawful and must end as rapidly as possible; settlements must be dismantled; reparations paid. Paragraph 229 found a breach of Article 3 CERD (racial segregation and apartheid).

items.title: Arrest warrants against Benjamin Netanyahu and Yoav Gallant
items.org: International Criminal Court, Pre-Trial Chamber I
items.note: Reasonable grounds to believe both bear responsibility for the war crime of starvation as a method of warfare and crimes against humanity of murder, persecution and other inhumane acts. A warrant was also issued against Hamas commander Mohammed Deif.

items.title: Situation in the State of Palestine
items.org: International Criminal Court, Office of the Prosecutor
items.note: The open investigation covering conduct in the West Bank, East Jerusalem and Gaza since 13 June 2014.

items.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina v. Serbia and Montenegro
items.note: The only ICJ ruling directly on the duty to prevent genocide. The obligation arises the moment a state learns of a serious risk, not once genocide is proven; it is a duty of conduct, and it is irrelevant whether full effort would have succeeded.

items.title: Prosecutor v. Akayesu (ICTR-96-4-T)
items.note: The foundational jurisprudence on inferring genocidal intent from a pattern of conduct and from dehumanising speech.

items.title: University of Bristol v Dr David Miller [2026] EAT 84
items.note: Appeal EA-2024-000324-RS. Lord Fairley KC, with Nick Aziz and Dr Gillian Smith MBE. Eight of nine grounds rejected; anti-Zionist belief in the formulation advanced held a protected philosophical belief, dismissal held direct discrimination. Compensation reduced by 50 per cent for contributory conduct.

items.title: HCJ 5555/18, Hasson v. Knesset (petitions against Basic Law: Israel — the Nation State of the Jewish People)
items.org: Supreme Court of Israel, sitting as the High Court of Justice
items.note: An extended bench of eleven justices rejected fifteen petitions by ten to one, President Esther Hayut holding that the Basic Law does not negate the state's democratic character. The sole dissent was that of Justice George Karra, the court's only Arab justice.

items.title: State of New South Wales v Farhat [2026] NSWSC 985
items.org: Supreme Court of New South Wales (Fagan J)
items.note: Refusal of an extended supervision order under the Terrorism (High Risk Offenders) Act 2017 (NSW). The court declined to take the meaning of antisemitism from the IHRA working definition, holding the text “so verbose and imprecise that it could not realistically be attributed to the ordinary, reasonably informed member of the Australian public” and “detached from the reality of the common usage and understanding of antisemitism in this country” (§21.9). The New South Wales Attorney General announced on 31 August 2026 that the State would not appeal.

items.title: Baldassi and Others v. France, applications nos. 15271/16 and six others
items.org: European Court of Human Rights (Fifth Section)
items.note: Unanimous finding that the criminal conviction of eleven activists for calling in supermarkets for a boycott of Israeli goods violated Article 10 of the Convention; EUR 7,380 awarded to each applicant. The Court held that a call to boycott is expression on a matter of public interest and distinguished Willem v. France (2009), where the applicant acted in the exercise of public authority as a mayor. Cited at Rebuttal 22.

items.title: NAACP v. Claiborne Hardware Co., 458 U.S. 886 (1982)
items.org: Supreme Court of the United States
items.note: Held that a politically motivated boycott is protected expression under the First Amendment, and that liability could not be imposed for peaceful advocacy of it. The domestic counterpart to Baldassi, and the authority on which several federal courts have enjoined state anti-boycott certification requirements. Cited at Rebuttal 22.

items.title: Obligations of Israel in relation to the Presence and Activities of the United Nations, Other International Organizations and Third States in and in relation to the Occupied Palestinian Territory
items.note: Advisory Opinion, General List No. 196 (UN doc. A/80/502), requested by General Assembly resolution 79/232. Unanimous on most findings, ten to one on the rest. Holds that Article 59 of the Fourth Geneva Convention obliges the occupying power to agree to and facilitate relief, that it must use all means at its disposal to see relief distributed fairly, and that UNRWA's capacity cannot be replicated or replaced on short notice. Recorded at §15.1A.

groups.label: United Nations bodies
groups.blurb: Commissions of inquiry, treaty bodies, special procedures and operational agencies. Mandated, methodologically documented, and published under institutional accountability.

items.title: Report of the Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the OPT (A/HRC/60/CRP.3)
items.note: The first UN body to find that Israel has committed genocide in Gaza, and that Herzog, Netanyahu and Gallant incited it. Chair: Navi Pillay.

items.title: Report of the Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the OPT
items.note: Second affirmative genocide finding, on the deliberate targeting of children. Chair: Srinivasan Muralidhar.

items.title: Anatomy of a Genocide (A/HRC/55/73)
items.org: UN Special Rapporteur on the OPT, Francesca Albanese
items.note: The first UN mandate-holder report to conclude that the threshold indicating genocide had been met.

items.title: Report on starvation and the right to food in Gaza
items.org: UN Special Rapporteur on the Right to Food, Michael Fakhri
items.note: Concluded that Israel was committing genocide by starvation.

items.title: Forcible displacement in the northern West Bank refugee camps
items.note: Found the displacement of 33,000+ Palestinians from Jenin, Nur Shams and Tulkarem during Operation Iron Wall to be large-scale, long-term and systematic, raising concerns of the crime against humanity of forcible transfer.

items.title: Report of the Special Committee to Investigate Israeli Practices
items.note: Found Israel's warfare methods in Gaza consistent with genocide, including the use of starvation as a weapon.

items.title: Humanitarian situation updates, occupied Palestinian territory
items.org: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
items.note: The operational casualty, displacement and access record. OCHA's verified fatality database covers 2008–2023; the post-October-2023 figures appear in situation updates pending full verification.

items.title: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification — Gaza analyses
items.note: The authoritative famine classification, including the confirmation of Famine (IPC Phase 5) conditions in Gaza governorates.

items.title: Health system attacks and casualty reporting, oPt
items.note: The Surveillance System for Attacks on Health Care (SSA) record, and WHO's independent assessment of Ministry of Health casualty data.

items.title: Situation reports, occupied Palestinian territory
items.note: Displacement, shelter and staff-casualty data, and the record of the funding and legislative campaign against the agency.

items.title: Damage assessments, Gaza Strip
items.note: Satellite-derived building damage assessments — the independent physical corroboration of the destruction figures.

items.title: Child casualty and grave-violations reporting
items.note: Including the Secretary-General's annual Children and Armed Conflict report, which listed Israeli forces for grave violations against children in June 2024.

items.title: Report of the UN Fact-Finding Mission on the Gaza Conflict (the Goldstone Report, A/HRC/12/48)
items.note: Documented the Dahiya Doctrine of deliberate disproportionality as policy rather than error.

items.title: Database of business enterprises involved in activities relating to Israeli settlements in the occupied Palestinian territory
items.org: UN Human Rights Office (OHCHR), mandated by HRC resolution 31/36
items.date: first published February 2020; updated June 2023 and July 2025
items.note: The only United Nations register of named companies with settlement-linked operations. The listing grew from 112 enterprises in 2020 to 158 in July 2025. It records listed activity, not a legal finding against any company.

items.title: Resolution 181 (II): Future Government of Palestine (the Partition Plan)
items.note: The territorial allocation against which every later land figure is measured: 56 per cent of Mandatory Palestine to a Jewish state, 43 per cent to an Arab state, Jerusalem under international administration.

items.title: “The essence of childhood has been destroyed”: Israel's deliberate targeting of Palestinian children in the Occupied Palestinian Territory since 7 October 2023
items.org: UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the OPT
items.note: Report A/HRC/62/CRP.2. Found the deliberate targeting of Palestinian children amounting to genocide and atrocity crimes in Gaza and war crimes in the West Bank, covering 7 October 2023 to 31 March 2026: at least 20,179 children killed and 44,143 injured.

items.title: Israel's discriminatory death penalty law marks grave human rights retrogression, UN anti-racism committee warns
items.org: UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination / OHCHR
items.note: Finds the Death Penalty for Terrorists Law racially discriminatory and an instance of segregation, applying de facto to Palestinians only, and calls on all States parties to ensure their resources are not used to enforce discriminatory policies.

items.title: Israel's death penalty law constitutes discriminatory regime of capital punishment: UN experts
items.note: Special Rapporteur on torture Alice Jill Edwards and others on hanging, the 90-day execution deadline and the prohibition on mandatory death sentences under the ICCPR.

items.title: IPC Famine Review Committee: famine classification for Gaza Governorate
items.note: Confirms famine (Phase 5) in Gaza Governorate as of 15 August 2025 — the first classification of famine in the Middle East and the first outside Africa. Records over 500,000 people in Phase 5, 1.07 million (54 per cent) in Phase 4 and 396,000 in Phase 3, projects the famine to Deir al-Balah and Khan Younis by the end of September 2025, and leaves northern Gaza unclassified for lack of access. Confirmed the same day by the World Health Organization.

items.title: Jose R. Martinez Cobo, Study of the Problem of Discrimination against Indigenous Populations (E/CN.4/Sub.2/1986/7 and Add.1-4)
items.org: UN Sub-Commission on Prevention of Discrimination and Protection of Minorities
items.note: The working description used in the UN system: historical continuity with pre-invasion societies, non-dominance in the present, and self-identification. It states a group's present relationship to a dominant power rather than a hereditary title to territory. Cited at 1.0 and at Rebuttal 23.

items.title: Gaza: impact on cultural heritage
items.note: Satellite-verified damage to 164 sites since 7 October 2023, including 14 religious sites, 128 buildings of historical or artistic interest, nine monuments and eight archaeological sites.

items.title: The Évian Conference, July 1938
items.note: Thirty-two states, the Dominican Republic the sole exception, and Britain's condition that Mandatory Palestine not be discussed.

items.title: Gaza Genocide: a collective crime (A/80/492)
items.org: Francesca Albanese, UN Special Rapporteur on the situation of human rights in the Palestinian territories occupied since 1967
items.note: Report to the General Assembly framing third-state diplomatic, military, humanitarian and economic support as participation in the crime rather than failure of policy, particularising Germany as the second-largest arms exporter of the period and the United Kingdom by reference to its surveillance flights over Gaza. Recorded at §15.1B.

groups.label: Human rights organisations
groups.blurb: Investigations with documented methodology by the organisations with the longest field presence. Israeli and Palestinian organisations are listed alongside the international ones because their findings converge.

items.title: A Threshold Crossed: Israeli Authorities and the Crimes of Apartheid and Persecution
items.note: The first apartheid finding by a major international organisation.

items.title: Extermination and Acts of Genocide: Israel Deliberately Depriving Palestinians in Gaza of Water
items.note: The genocide determination on water deprivation grounds.

items.title: Israel's Apartheid Against Palestinians: Cruel System of Domination and Crime Against Humanity
items.note: 278 pages compiled over four years.

items.title: 'You Feel Like You Are Subhuman': Israel's Genocide Against Palestinians in Gaza
items.note: Amnesty's affirmative genocide determination.

items.title: Erasing Anything Palestinian
items.note: Found a state-led campaign of ethnic cleansing in the West Bank and named Netanyahu, Ben-Gvir, Katz, Smotrich and Strock.

items.title: This is Apartheid: A Regime of Jewish Supremacy from the Jordan River to the Mediterranean Sea
items.note: The Israeli organisation's apartheid finding, covering all territory under Israeli control.

items.title: Our Genocide
items.note: B'Tselem's genocide determination, published simultaneously with Physicians for Human Rights Israel's.

items.title: Statistics on Palestinians and Israelis killed
items.note: The longest continuous independently maintained fatality database for the occupied territories, with per-person records.

items.title: Genocide in Gaza — the destruction of the health system
items.note: The medical profession's genocide finding, from inside Israeli civil society.

items.title: The Perimeter: Soldiers' testimonies from the Gaza Buffer Zone 2023–2024
items.note: Dozens of IDF testimonies documenting the razing of roughly 16% of the Gaza Strip to create a kill zone at least a kilometre deep.

items.title: Law enforcement on Israeli civilians in the West Bank — data sheets
items.note: Two decades of Israeli police file outcomes: over 93% of settler-violence investigations closed without indictment.

items.title: Legal analyses and submissions on the occupation, apartheid and genocide
items.note: The oldest Palestinian human rights organisation (founded 1979), an ICJ and ICC intervenor.

items.title: Field documentation and casualty investigations, Gaza
items.org: Al Mezan Center for Human Rights
items.note: Gaza-based field documentation of individual incidents.

items.title: Casualty and detention documentation
items.note: Weekly documented reporting from Gaza since 1995.

items.title: Child fatality and detention monitoring
items.note: The specialist record on child killings, arrest and military detention.

items.title: Verified statement and incident documentation
items.note: Independent verification and cataloguing of the most probative ministerial and military statements.

items.title: Field reporting from Gaza's hospitals
items.note: MSF has independently described the conduct in Gaza as genocide.

items.title: Reports on Gaza and the occupied territory
items.note: Including the water and aid-access analyses underpinning the starvation findings.

items.title: Reports on settlement expansion
items.note: The Israeli monitoring project on settlement construction, outposts and land seizure.

items.title: Statistics on Palestinian political prisoners and administrative detention
items.org: Addameer Prisoner Support and Human Rights Association
items.note: The cumulative record of detention under Israeli military order: more than 800,000 Palestinians detained since 1967, roughly 20% of the population of the occupied territory.

items.title: Statistics on house demolitions in the occupied territories
items.note: Compiled from the Israeli Ministry of Interior, the Jerusalem Municipality, the Civil Administration, OCHA and field work: roughly 52,000 homes demolished in the Nakba and more than 55,000 structures in the occupied territory since 1967.

items.title: Home demolitions in East Jerusalem, 1967–2018
items.note: 5,000 homes demolished since 1967, of which 1,706 between 2000 and 2017, displacing 9,422 people including 5,443 children.

items.title: Exclusion and observation decisions, Government Pension Fund Global
items.org: Norges Bank Investment Management, on the advice of the Council on Ethics
items.note: The world's largest sovereign wealth fund, and the most closely watched single test of the settlement-business listings. Source for the divestment record, alongside KLP, PFZW and AkademikerPension.

items.title: Corporate involvement in the occupation — company database
items.note: Independent Israeli research centre documenting the commercial infrastructure of the occupation, settlement industry and control of the Palestinian population. Predates and feeds the OHCHR database.

items.title: Israel Passes Mandatory Death Penalty for Palestinians Convicted of Terrorism
items.note: Provisions, the 96 per cent military-court conviction rate recorded by B'Tselem, and the reactions of the Council of Europe, Human Rights Watch and the US State Department.

items.title: Genocide Watch Gaza Report, July 2026
items.note: Places Gaza simultaneously at Stages 8 (persecution), 9 (extermination) and 10 (denial) of Gregory Stanton's ten-stage model, and addresses Hamas's attacks on Israeli civilians in the same report.

items.title: CPJ, partners file emergency motion to Israeli Supreme Court seeking independent media access to Gaza
items.note: Filed with the Foreign Press Association, Reporters Without Borders and the Union of Journalists in Israel. Records the ban on independent international press access to Gaza at more than 900 days.

items.title: RSF appeals to Israeli Supreme Court against the media blackout imposed on Gaza
items.note: The petition record on foreign press access, including the seven deferrals granted to the state in the petition's first year.

items.title: US Sanctions ICC President Tomoko Akane
items.note: Records the 18 August 2026 designations of the Court's President and a senior trial lawyer, bringing the total to nine of eighteen judges, both Deputy Prosecutors and the former Prosecutor.

items.title: Internal Fight: Palestinian Abuses in Gaza and the West Bank
items.note: Record of the 2007 factional killings, finding that more Palestinians died in internal Palestinian fighting that year (at least 490) than from Israeli attacks (at least 396), and that both Hamas and Fatah forces committed summary executions and torture (§18.10).

items.title: 'Strangling Necks': Abductions, torture and summary killings of Palestinians by Hamas forces during the 2014 Gaza/Israel conflict
items.note: Documents the extrajudicial execution of at least 23 Palestinians by Hamas forces during the 2014 conflict, including six men publicly executed outside the al-Omari mosque on 22 August 2014 (§18.10).

items.title: "Two Authorities, One Way, Zero Dissent": Arbitrary Arrest and Torture Under the Palestinian Authority and Hamas
items.note: Two-year investigation across 86 cases and 147 interviews finding that torture practised by both the Palestinian Authority and Hamas may amount to a crime against humanity (§18.10).

items.title: Israeli strike on a media tent outside al-Shifa Hospital kills Anas al-Sharif and five other journalists
items.note: Records the strike of 10 August 2025 and the six men killed, the Israeli military's assertion that al-Sharif headed a Hamas cell, the absence of any case offered for the other five, and CPJ's own warning of July 2025 that al-Sharif was the subject of a smear campaign. CPJ's database records more than 190 journalists and media workers killed since October 2023.

items.title: Human Rights and other Civil Society Groups Urge United Nations to Respect Human Rights in the Fight Against Antisemitism
items.org: Human Rights Watch and 103 other organisations
items.note: Open letter to UN Secretary-General António Guterres and High Representative Miguel Ángel Moratinos urging the United Nations not to endorse or adopt the IHRA working definition, and naming the Jerusalem Declaration on Antisemitism and the Nexus Document as alternatives. Signatories include the Israeli organisations B'Tselem and Breaking the Silence and the American Jewish organisation Americans for Peace Now (§21.9).

items.title: Petition: Don't let Israel define antisemitism
items.note: Calls on Australian governments and institutions to reject the IHRA definition and to adopt the Australian Human Rights Commission's National Anti-Racism Framework instead. Publishes the Australian adoption record: AHPRA, the Commonwealth Ombudsman and the Australian Government have adopted it; the ABC and SBS have rejected it (§21.9).

items.title: Letter Urging Inclusion of the IHRA Working Definition of Antisemitism in the UN Action Plan
items.org: Jewish communal and civil society organisations (list published by the Anti-Defamation League)
items.note: The counter-letter to the same two recipients, signed by more than 160 organisations and individuals, describing the definition as “an indispensable tool to understand and fight antisemitism”, “one that can be used entirely consistently with fundamental human rights standards” (§21.9). Recorded so that the competing position is available in its own words.

items.title: Importing Occupation: Europe's Complicity in Palestinian Dispossession through Settlement Agricultural Trade
items.note: Four-year investigation of more than 30,000 Israeli export documents: more than 17 per cent of 5,900 shipments to Europe between October 2017 and February 2026 contained settlement-origin products, against the 2.23 per cent previously claimed.

items.title: Palestinians call on Ed Sheeran to cancel his compromised US tour
items.note: The call to the headline act and to opening artists, audience members and crew, with a 15 September addendum responding to his statement of that day.

items.title: Victory for staff as Royal Ballet and Opera pulls Tel Aviv production
items.note: The open letter signed by 182 members of the company, and the cancellation of the 2026 Tosca at the Israeli Opera.

items.title: The UK Royal Air Force's surveillance flights over the Occupied Palestinian Territory examined
items.note: The underlying flight-tracking study: sortie counts by month, duration and administration, and the 24 flights in the fortnight before the Nuseirat assault.

items.title: Did Britain fly at least 623 spy flights over Gaza?
items.note: The extended count to 25 July 2025: at least 606 RAF flights plus 17 flown by US defence contractors.

items.title: UK Gaza spy flights may hold evidence of attacks on civilians
items.note: The Ministry of Defence confirms it holds footage, including from a flight relevant to the World Central Kitchen convoy strike, and refuses disclosure on national-security grounds.

items.title: Briefing: concerns regarding Palantir Technologies and NHS data systems
items.note: Clinician-led briefing on the Federated Data Platform, the procurement route and the company's other contracts.

items.title: Israeli Government threat to ban British charities from humanitarian work in Palestine
items.note: Statement on the 8 September 2026 ministerial letter, opening with the killing of eight-year-old Wafaa Akila and her father, characterising the letter as retaliation for the settlement trade bans, and calling on the British government to stop treating Israel as an ally or as a state that abides by international law. Recorded at §15.3C.

items.title: Gaza: Israel Curbs Aid, Kills Civilians During Ceasefire
items.note: Seven months into the ceasefire: 856 killed and 2,463 wounded since it began, weekly aid deliveries down from 4,200 trucks to 590 after the 28 February crossing closures, 18,500 patients awaiting medical evacuation and 19 of 37 hospitals partially functional.

items.title: A Registry of Israeli Genocidal Statements on Gaza

items.title: Red Flag Alerts and statements on incitement
items.note: Including the Red Flag Alert on Israel in Lebanon (March 2026) and the statement on Ben-Gvir's incitement (1 September 2026).

items.title: Ten Stages of Genocide assessments — Gaza
items.note: Assessed Gaza at Stages 8 (Persecution), 9 (Extermination) and 10 (Denial) simultaneously.

items.title: Statements by Israeli Officials, Soldiers and Civil Society on Genocide
items.note: Compilation of official and informal translations, each with the Hebrew original and a link to the recording or post it was taken from. Assembled as the genocide case was filed at the International Court of Justice.

items.title: Discriminatory Laws in Israel — database
items.org: Adalah — The Legal Center for Arab Minority Rights in Israel
items.note: Catalogues more than 65 Israeli laws that discriminate directly or indirectly against Palestinian citizens of Israel and Palestinians in the occupied territory, each with its statutory text and a note on its effect.

items.title: FEC itemised receipts: Kraft Group LLC contributions, 2016-2026
items.note: The primary filings behind §15.12: five contributions totalling $3,000,000 to the United Democracy Project between 15 July 2022 and 26 February 2026, $150,000 to DMFI PAC in 2021, and $1,000,000 to the 58th Presidential Inaugural Committee in 2016.

items.title: FEC committee profile: United Democracy Project (C00799031)
items.note: AIPAC's super political action committee. Receipts of $35.9m, $87.2m and $107.5m across the 2022, 2024 and 2026 cycles, independent expenditures of $26.1m, $37.9m and $50.9m, and $51,555,842.93 transferred in from AIPAC's own treasury.

items.title: ISPT0372 - Church of Saint Porphyrius, 19 October 2023
items.note: Names at least 23 civilians killed, including ten children, eight women and five men of the al-Amash, al-Souri and al-Tarazi families.

items.note: Public-domain aggregation of Gaza Ministry of Health, Government Media Office and West Bank figures. The source of the monthly and cumulative series on the Data view.

items.note: Build pipeline, schemas and caveats on completeness for the datasets above.

items.title: Israel–Palestine conflict event data

items.title: Journalist casualty database

items.title: Palestinians killed since 1948 — World Refugee Day statistical release
items.note: The only cumulative figure published by the Palestinian statistical authority: 136,000 Palestinians killed since 1948. The period-by-period basis has not been published.

items.title: Arms Transfers Database and Trends in International Arms Transfers, 2024
items.note: The standard open register of state-to-state major-weapons transfers. Source for the supplier shares used in the complicity ledger: 66 per cent of Israeli major arms imports in 2020–2024 from the United States and 33 per cent from Germany.

items.title: Security Council — Veto List (Quick Links)
items.note: The complete record of vetoes cast in the Security Council since 1946, by member and by draft resolution. Source for the veto wall: 49 United States vetoes of draft resolutions concerning Israel and Palestine, the largest single-subject block in the Council's history.

items.title: Trends in International Arms Transfers, 2025
items.note: The United States at 42 per cent of global exports of major arms for 2021-25; 68 per cent of Israel's imports supplied by the United States and 31 per cent by Germany; Israel the seventh largest exporter at 4.4 per cent.

items.title: Middle East Overview, May 2026
items.org: ACLED (Armed Conflict Location and Event Data Project)
items.note: Event-level conflict data recording April 2026 as the deadliest month of the year in Gaza, with more than 140 deaths and violent events up 35 per cent on March, and Israeli territorial control at roughly 58 per cent of the Strip.

items.title: Bad News From Israel and More Bad News From Israel
items.org: Glasgow University Media Group (Greg Philo and Mike Berry)
items.note: The foundational audience and content studies on Western media coverage of the conflict.

items.title: The Hundred Years' War on Palestine
items.note: Documents the Zionist movement's own institutional use of the vocabulary of colonisation.

items.title: The Ethnic Cleansing of Palestine
items.note: Archive-based account of Plan Dalet and the 1948 expulsions.

items.title: The Birth of the Palestinian Refugee Problem Revisited

items.title: Zionism in the Age of the Dictators
items.note: Source for the Haavara Agreement and Kareski affair material, corroborated against Institute for Palestine Studies and German Foreign Ministry archive records.

items.title: United States Spending on Israel's Military Operations and Related U.S. Operations in the Region
